native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA on the forms of capital in hundred-year time slices, the Younger Bronze Age opens at a pronounced peak rather than a low point: PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.447) lies about 3.0 units above the mean of the 1000–500 BCE slices (+1.412) and exceeds every subsequent horizon by +2.3 to +3.7 units, then declines monotonically-ish to ~+0.8 by 600–500 BCE. With PC1 oriented so higher values mean more capital (positive loadings on copper–gold +0.78, depots/hoards +0.65, daggers +0.51, house size +0.43, monuments +0.39), the 1100 BCE outlier is driven by a short-lived spike in hoarding and metal wealth (ZCU_AU +2.85, ZHort 3.38, ZDolch +1.10, Zhausgr +1.65, ZMonument +1.35 at 1100 BCE) that collapses from 1000 BCE onward; routine-agricultural indicators (sickles, axes/celts, pottery form) remain flat or low. A YBA-only PCA sensitivity (excluding the YBA-invariant ZSichel and ZKeform) reproduces the same pattern with even larger contrast (PC1(1100) = +5.35 vs later mean −0.89), confirming that the beginning of the Younger Bronze Age represents a high point of accumulated capital not sustained through 1000–500 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (39 century rows, BCE 500-4300); variance-checked all 12 Z-indicators (none zero-variance in full table; ZSichel and ZKeform constant within YBA and excluded only in the YBA-only sensitivity); standardized and ran correlation-matrix PCA via numpy SVD on the full 39-row table as primary; fixed PC1 sign so ZHort loading is positive (higher PC1 = more capital); extracted PC1 at 1100, 1000, 900, 800, 700, 600, 500 BCE; computed the 1100-vs-1000-500 difference (+3.035) and per-slice differences (+2.30 to +3.67); repeated PCA on YBA rows only as sensitivity (+6.241, same direction); pollen openness file excluded from computation. Outputs: pc1_by_century.csv, pc1_loadings.csv.
